title: Resolve zombie-session billing & prefix-ghosting for resumed streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem summary:

We observe a class of billing anomalies where long-lived websocket sessions that are force-truncated server-side (due to memory pressure or operator-driven restart) later re-establish with resumed fragments. During resume/backfill the metering pipeline sometimes attributes tokens twice or leaves provisional credits unfinalized, producing "ghost" prefix charges and/or orphaned debits on customer invoices. This ticket scopes an end-to-end reconciliation and hardening plan to eliminate: duplicate token attribution on resumed streams, phantom prefix accounting ("prefix-ghosting"), and quota leakage when provisional credits are not reconciled after server-initiated truncations.

Key failure modes observed:
- Server-initiated truncation that emits a terminal frame but client reconnects with an overlapping fragment range; provisional credits already consumed are re-allocated (double charge).
- Backfilled fragments delivered out-of-order across reconnections result in credits attributed to ephemeral session IDs that are abandoned (ghost charges).
- Rate limiter rehydration during resume treats the resumed session as a new session and applies both old and new quotas, allowing bursts that bypass intended limits.
- Ledger anchors are created on partial checkpoints and never reconciled when the session regenerates under a different proxy path, leaving orphan ledger entries.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
- Deterministic, idempotent token attribution semantics for any resume/truncate/reconnect sequence.
- No duplicate debits in production billing audits for resumed sessions (end-to-end tests + audit runbook).
- Rate limiter and quota state reflect only outstanding active credits; resumed sessions must not gain additional quota beyond permitted windows.
- Monitoring: dashboard showing count of resumed-sessions, reconciliation failures, and delta between provisional and finalized debits; thresholds alerting on >0.1% rate of mismatches.

Design proposal (high-level):
1) Monotonic fragment sequence numbers + session provenance hash: require that every fragment contains a monotonic fragment_seq and a session_provenance_hash computed by the proxy chain. Use this to identify backfilled content vs replays.
2) Provisional credits with anchor tokens: on first receipt of a fragment, create a provisional ledger entry with a provisional_id and attach anchor_checksum. Do not finalize until a terminal checkpoint or an idempotent anchor reconciliation is performed.
3) Resume reconciliation protocol: when a reconnect occurs, the client/proxy supplies last_ack_seq and prior_provisional_ids. The broker compares anchor_checksum and fragment_seq ranges to detect overlap. Overlapping fragments reconcile by marking matching provisional_ids as final and discarding duplicate provisional debits.
4) Immutable anchor ledger with tombstones: anchors remain immutable; if an anchor is superseded by a resurrection with a different provenance, mark old anchors as tombstones and offset debits using an explicit refund entry to maintain auditability.
5) Rate limiter binding: bind speculative provisional credits to a logical session fingerprint; on resume only the delta of unfinalized credits is available for consumption; finalized credits do not increase quota.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict monotonic sequencing increases client/proxy requirements; alternative is server-side heuristics. We opted for explicit sequencing to make reconciliation deterministic and auditable.
- Leaving provisional credits open longer increases memory and state retention; mitigations include soft TTLs and prioritized reconciliation sweeps.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Spike (2d): prototype reconciliation library that accepts fragment_seq ranges and provisional_id lists and outputs reconciliation actions (finalize, discard, refund). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/recon-proto/pull/42.
- Server changes (4d): add anchor_checksum verification and provisional ledger writes in the streaming ingress path. Implement tombstone/refund entries. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2387.
- Proxy/client SDK changes (3d): include fragment_seq and prior_provisional_ids in resume handshake. Update SDKs and capture in streaming SDK changelog. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-sdk/pull/101.
- Rate limiter update (2d): bind provisional credits to session fingerprint and prevent quota amplification on resume.
- E2E tests & audit harness (3d): synthetic test runner that simulates truncation/resume patterns and asserts ledger invariants. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/stream-recon/stream-recon-overview
- Gradual rollout (2w): feature-flag gating, canary across 10% of traffic, monitor reconciliation_failure_rate and customer complaints for billing anomalies.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for reconciliation library covering overlap, disjoint, exact-match, and out-of-order backfills.
- Integration tests with local proxy to assert idempotency across replays and reconnections.
- Synthetic fault injection in staging to simulate operator truncations and proxy restarts.
- Backfill audit job against last 30 days of ledgers to identify and auto-correct orphaned anchors; run read-only first, then corrective mode.

Rollout and monitoring plan:
- Feature-flag default OFF; enable for non-billing customers first (internal & dev tenants) for 48 hours.
- Canary to 10% with reconciliation metrics enabled at runtime-1.32. If reconciliation_failure_rate < 0.05% and no increase in customer billing complaints for 48h, expand to 50% then 100% over 7 days.
- Post-rollout: run automatic ledger audit sweep nightly for 14 days and compare delta to pre-rollout baseline.

Open questions / blockers:
- Do older clients need a compatibility shim if they cannot supply prior_provisional_ids? Proposal: server attempts probabilistic reconciliation using fragment_seq and checksum, but will fall back to delayed TTL-based finalization (risking transient provisional debits).
- Operational cost: how many provisional entries can we sustain in the ledger TTL window before compaction is required? Need load test numbers.

References & artifacts:
- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/recon-proto/pull/42
- Server PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2387
- Streaming SDK PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/stream-sdk/pull/101
- Design notes (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Resumed+Stream+Reconciliation
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/stream-recon/stream-recon-overview

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Unit & integration tests pass in CI with 100% coverage for reconciliation code paths.
- Nightly audit job report shows zero net duplicate debits across canary tenants for 7 consecutive days.
- No increase in customer-reported billing anomalies during canary window.
- Documentation & SDK changelogs published prior to full rollout.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marco Jensen: Spike started. Built prototype reconciliation library and tested basic overlap cases. Found a race where two proxies reconnecting simultaneously can both try to finalize the same provisional_id — added optimistic compare-and-swap on ledger finalization.

2026-03-04 - Priya Shah (SRE): Load-tested provisional entry retention at 50k concurrent provisional anchors; memory footprint acceptable but GC spikes observed. Recommended TTL of 6 hours with compaction sweep every 30m.
2026-03-06 - Dan Liu (Billing PM): Confirmed acceptance criteria; requested nightly audit job output to include candidate refunds for manual review before auto-applying.
